strengths: Novel application of frequency domain compression to decoder-only LLM KV caches, claimed as first work in this area
Parameter-efficient design with no additional learnable modules, avoiding ~2B parameters for 7B models
Clear empirical evidence of low-frequency energy concentration in KV states across decoder layers (Figure 1)
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple models (LLaMA-2-7b, LLaMA-3-8b), benchmarks (PG-19, Proof-pile, LongBench, Needle-in-a-Haystack), and baselines
Practical efficiency: negligible compression overhead (<0.64% at 32K tokens) with linear decoding time growth vs quadratic for full attention
Strong Needle-in-a-Haystack results (84.2% accuracy for LLaMA-2, 90.7% for LLaMA-3) demonstrating effective long-range information retrieval
Minimal performance degradation within original context window compared to compression baselines
Effective context extension demonstrated (4K to 64K, 16x scaling)
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification: Why does energy concentrate in low frequencies for KV states? What information do frequency components encode? No mechanistic explanation provided
Domain-specific performance limitations: Significant underperformance on Proof-pile at longer contexts (2.72 vs 2.50 for LongLoRA at 32K). Limited analysis of which domains/task types fail
Modest empirical improvements: Gains over baselines are often within noise margins; Table 2 shows mixed LongBench results with some task regressions

Methodological concerns not addressed: (1) No justification for DCT vs FFT or other transforms, (2) Position embedding handling (pre-RoPE compression) lacks rigorous validation, (3) Retaining ratio γ=0.5 and sink tokens S=4 chosen without ablation

Limited experimental scope: Only 7B/8B models tested; no evidence frequency concentration pattern holds at different scales (13B, 70B+). Only LLaMA family evaluated; generalization to other architectures unclear
Incomplete ablations: Missing ablations on sink token count, number of compression iterations, frequency range importance, and sensitivity to hyperparameters beyond Figure 4
Presentation issues: Figure 1 uses varying y-axis scales making comparison difficult, notation sometimes confusing, key design decisions in brief paragraphs
Reproducibility concerns: No code availability mentioned, some baseline results from prior work with potentially different training settings, incomplete random seed/variance reporting

strengths: Well-motivated frequency-domain analysis with strong empirical evidence (Figure 1) showing energy concentration in low-frequency KV components
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse benchmarks (language modeling, understanding, generation) with consistent improvements and SOTA results on multiple tasks
Parameter-free and architecture-agnostic design requiring no model modifications, with significant practical benefits (40.89% training time reduction, <0.3% compression overhead)
Strong empirical results including 256K token extrapolation from 8K training and robustness to aggressive compression (γ=1%)
Thorough empirical analysis including perturbation experiments, ablation studies, compression overhead analysis, and head-wise investigation supporting design choices
Technical soundness with clear method description, correct mathematical formulations, and detailed implementation enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily applies well-known DCT-based frequency filtering to KV cache compression without algorithmic innovation or new insights

Weak theoretical grounding: lacks principled justification for why DCT is optimal, no information-theoretic analysis, and no investigation of semantic information preservation across frequency components

Domain-specific limitations: acknowledged performance degradation on Proof-pile (mathematical content) suggests the method may not generalize to all content types, contradicting claims of general applicability
Methodological concerns with ad-hoc design choices: retaining ratio γ=0.5 and sink size S=4 lack principled justification; sensitivity to compression-before-RoPE ordering suggests brittleness
Limited architectural diversity: evaluation restricted to LLaMA-2/3 only; no exploration of Mistral, Qwen, or other popular models; unclear scalability to 70B+ parameters
Incomplete ablation studies: missing task-specific frequency analysis, limited investigation of cumulative multi-stage compression loss, and perturbation robustness only at 1% word replacement
Hyperparameter selection lacks principled guidance: no clear methodology for selecting compression parameters across different scenarios or models
Fair comparison concerns: FreqKV requires training while some baselines are training-free; different methods may use different fine-tuning procedures despite stated equivalence

strengths: Well-motivated core observation: convincing empirical evidence that KV states exhibit strong energy concentration in low-frequency DCT components (Figure 1), supported by perturbation analysis (Figure 2) and summarization experiments (Table 1)
Parameter-free and architecture-agnostic design: no additional trainable parameters or architectural modifications required, enabling broad applicability across model variants

Comprehensive and strong empirical validation: SOTA on most LongBench tasks, only method maintaining performance at 16K beyond original window (Table 4, RULER), substantial improvements on long-context generation (LongGenBench)
Remarkable extrapolation capability: extends LLaMA-2-7B from 8K to 256K tokens (64×) while maintaining stable perplexity, demonstrating effective iterative compression strategy
Significant practical efficiency: 40.89% faster training and 44.19% less memory than full fine-tuning (Table 7), with negligible compression overhead (<0.3%) during inference
Robust under aggressive compression: remains stable even at extreme γ=1% retaining ratio (Table 3) while other methods degrade sharply, demonstrating method robustness

Thorough experimental rigor: extensive ablations (Appendix F), head-wise analysis (Appendix B), careful comparison with variants (Dropping), and analysis of key design choices (rescaling factor, RoPE integration)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations: Figure 3 clearly illustrates frequency compression pipeline, Figure 4 heatmaps effectively demonstrate failure modes of baselines
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core technique is standard DCT-based low-pass filtering applied to KV cache; the innovation is somewhat incremental and primarily engineering-focused rather than algorithmic

Significant performance degradation on formula-heavy text: Proof-pile results (Table 9) show FreqKV trails LongLoRA substantially at 32K context (2.72 vs 2.50), revealing fundamental limitation where local details of symbolic content are critical

Incomplete semantic understanding: while Figure 2 demonstrates low-frequency robustness, limited analysis of what semantic information is actually preserved; beyond summarization (Table 1), sparse investigation of which task types benefit from global vs. local information

Weak performance on specific task categories: few-shot learning tasks show minimal gains or slight regression (Table 3: TRECL 56.0 vs 75.5 full cache), lacking analysis of which downstream tasks degrade most under compression

RoPE integration lacks theoretical justification: decision to compress before rather than after RoPE is empirically motivated (Table 8) but conceptually unclear; explanation of avoiding 'out-of-bound position embeddings' needs rigorous technical argument; potential fragility with alternative position encodings

Hyperparameter choices inadequately justified: default γ=0.5 not well motivated (ablations show γ=0.75 improves performance), sink size S=4 appears arbitrary with limited sensitivity analysis (only three γ values tested), missing guidance on selection

Theory-practice gap: limited explanation of why DCT specifically is appropriate for transformer KV states versus alternatives (FFT, wavelets); insufficient analysis of relationship between observed frequency properties and underlying attention mechanics

Comparison fairness issues: baseline OOM at extended lengths (Table 2) complicates direct comparison; some results reproduced by authors (marked with *) potentially introducing inconsistencies; no direct comparison with position interpolation methods under identical conditions
Missing failure mode analysis: limited guidance on when practitioners should prefer alternative approaches; few-shot learning degradation suggests domain-dependent utility not fully characterized
Position encoding claims need stronger support: Section 3.4 claims about avoiding position extrapolation deserve more rigorous technical justification rather than empirical verification alone
